text: Found it — the schema declares tags as a plain string instead of an array, which is why the model returns a comma-separated string while the dashboard expects a list. The fix is to change it to an array of strings capped at three entries with an updated description. I should also check if there are other consumers of this schema in index.ts or elsewhere, though this isn't a git repo so I can't check history.
The cause is visible in the schema: `tags` is declared as `z.string()` with a description asking for comma-separated text, so the model is asked for one string. I'll change it to an array of strings.

I'm noting the evidence: the schema definition in flows.ts, its use in the ai.generate call, and the description text itself calling for comma-separated values, while being upfront that I verified this through type checking rather than running the flow live. The bug was in the output schema for `summarizeTicket`: `tags` was declared as `z.string()`, so the model was constrained to return one comma-separated string. I changed it to `z.array(z.string())` in `src/flows.ts` line 8, and the project still type-checks. I did not run the flow against the live model, since that needs an API key. `answer.json` is written to the project root with the details.
